question: Q1
why: Request shows $279bn of supply commitments at Q2 FY2027 with $92bn scheduled for the rest of FY2027; even pure run-off leaves about $187bn, far above rung 5's $125bn floor. C1 repeats the $279bn already shown.

question: Q2

candidates.why: Broadcom's $10.8bn quarterly AI revenue, largely custom accelerators, annualises above $40bn; the judge would likely leave rung 1.
A $16.0bn next-quarter AI guide from the main custom-ASIC vendor implies calendar-2026 custom-silicon spend well above $40bn.
Trainium at multi-billion scale shows real 2026 spend but does not alone cross $40bn.
A growth rate through 2033 gives no 2026 level.
New Broadcom programs ramp from late 2026, adding mostly to 2027, little to the 2026 total.

why: Two unquantified items cannot place spending below $40bn; the judge reads absence of figures as a low figure. The measure has no defined source or buyer scope. Broadcom's AI revenue and guide would likely move it above rung 1.

question: Q3

candidates.why: Micron's fiscal Q3 revenue more than four times the prior year adds a second quarter of price-driven growth; same rung.
Prices easing by 2028 says nothing against a 2026 average far above 2025.

why: Shown: Micron revenue up 379%, data-center gross margin 41% to 90%, DGX Spark up 75% on memory costs, no balance date. That puts the 2026 average rise well above 30%; candidates mostly repeat shown NVIDIA margin items.

question: Q4

candidates.why: Precedent that Nvidia already signed a residual-value guarantee (SB Energy Ohio) makes a signed platform guarantee more credible; same Yes.
Nvidia's own project-by-project, up-to-25% support confirms intent, but shows guarantees per deal rather than one platform agreement.
Burry's attack on Nvidia's residual-value data adds to lender doubt; may weaken Yes slightly, not overturn it.

why: Yes is a reasonable forecast from the proposal, six partners and lenders demanding guarantees. But the ladder assumes one platform-wide guarantee while support is per deal, and drops the focus's amount; the Ohio precedent was not shown.
